isolateRealRoots.explanation: Find every real root of one univariate polynomial with exact rational coefficients. SymPy isolates the roots with sympy.intervals(strict=True); the result is a list of disjoint closed rational intervals, each holding exactly one distinct root, with its multiplicity. A rational root is published as an exact point interval. The host then re-proves completeness, disjointness, width and multiplicity from the coefficients alone using a square-free decomposition and Sturm sequences, so a missing or mislabelled root is refused.
pitfalls: Coefficients are literal exact fractions in descending powers; there is no expression syntax, so write x^2 - 2 as ["1", "0", "-2"], including the zero coefficients.
An interval is not a decimal approximation of the root unless you choose to read it as one; a point interval means the root is exactly that rational number.
Complex roots are counted but never located, and nothing is claimed about the numerical conditioning of whatever problem produced the coefficients.
Only SymPy 1.14.0 is accepted; a different release is refused rather than assumed compatible.

examples.purpose: The two irrational roots of x^2 - 2 isolated to width 1/1000.
Exact point roots -2 (multiplicity 2) and 1 (multiplicity 3) plus a complex pair.

fields.explanation: Isolate all real roots of one rational polynomial. Give the coefficients as exact fraction strings from the highest power down and, optionally, the widest isolating interval you accept. Results are a table of rational intervals with multiplicities, a native summary and an independent host verification record.

/properties/version.explanation: Required Schemaxis document contract schemaxis.sympy/1. It is an input-format version, separate from the qualified native SymPy 1.14.0 runtime.

/properties/operation.explanation: Choose isolateRealRoots, the only operation: exact real-root isolation with multiplicities and a host-checked certificate.

/properties/coefficients.explanation: Required list of 2 to 13 exact rational coefficients in descending powers, so the list length is the degree plus one (degree 1 to 12). The first entry multiplies x^degree and must be nonzero; interior zero coefficients are written out ("0"). Each entry is a string of an optional sign, digits and an optional /denominator, at most 40 digits each, for example "-3/2" or "7". Fractions need not be reduced; the plan shows them reduced.
/properties/coefficients.defaultMeaning: There is no default: the coefficients are required.

/properties/coefficients/items.explanation: One exact rational coefficient. Decimals (0.5), exponents (1e3), names (x, pi, sqrt(2)), arithmetic (1+1), spaces and non-ASCII digits are refused as invalid data; they are never evaluated. Write 1/2, not 0.5.

/properties/maximumIntervalWidth.explanation: Largest allowed width of each published interval, as an exact positive fraction between 1/10^30 and 1. Narrower intervals take slightly more native work and have longer endpoints. Exact point roots have width zero whatever you choose. The host rejects any interval wider than this.
/properties/maximumIntervalWidth.units: Same units as the root (x has no unit here).
